summary: My advisory is repaired as proposed — the condition-1 clause now reads 'This file existing, or an ACCEPT verdict, is not owner recording. It does not authorize a security-complete claim', keeping the security-complete sentence alongside the new foreclosure. Beyond that, the trust boundary carries substantive repairs I did not request and would have raised had I looked harder at v1: its first threat entry was a scope recital rather than a threat, and its first mitigation likewise. v2 replaces them with an actual threat — 'Substituted, unsigned, expired, revoked, rollbacked, or wrong-platform root/index/core/component bytes at first install' — and an actual mitigation that refuses those bytes on the scoped DR-G08 surfaces. The doctor threat entry is also updated to absorb the D-038 adoption while preserving the distinction I verified when reviewing D-038: host acts stay unexercisable 'until the host-effect contract has a live owner-recorded instance (FC-C1). D-038 recorded the accepted design contract; that is not FC-C1.' The boundary arithmetic still holds at seven against adopted D-030.

I record this as a miss of mine at v1: I verified the boundary enumeration arithmetically against D-030 and did not test whether the entries inside each boundary were of the kind their field names promise.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: d9084d4dc16bb450562520c2bed77cd80129bc65763f7ec2f55f3476c8989f52 both times. No drift.

ACCEPT is foreclosed as owner recording, which was my advisory and is the axis that matters most while I am issuing an ACCEPT on the artifact, and most of all on a row where the coordinator is a named co-owner.

The boundary arithmetic still holds and still matches its governing decision. boundaryCount is 7 and the boundaries array holds 7; familiesNamedByD030 holds 7 and matches adopted D-030's enumeration of command, input, process/protocol, state, output, platform and trust. The seven boundary ids map one-to-one onto the seven families.

The trust boundary's contents now match their field names, which is the substantive improvement in this version. A threatsTreated entry that recites gate membership is not a threat, and a previewMitigations entry that recites scope is not a mitigation; both are now populated with the thing the field promises. The new threat enumerates six concrete attack shapes at first install — substituted, unsigned, expired, revoked, rollbacked, wrong-platform — against the four named byte classes.

The doctor threat entry absorbs the D-038 adoption without over-reading it, and I checked this against my own D-038 review. It states host acts are unexercisable 'until the host-effect contract has a live owner-recorded instance (FC-C1). D-038 recorded the accepted design contract; that is not FC-C1.' That is exactly the distinction adopted D-038 draws in its own clause 2, and exactly the basis on which I consented to it.
The actor split is still named and still bounded: 'Host-under-instruction is outside DR-105. Component tails stay in DR-105… This TM names that split; it does not replace that contract.'
Wave-through is still rejected in a dedicated field and defeated in substance by the seven enumerated boundaries.
The open frame is intact, including the rule I singled out at v1: a D-002 successor that adds a boundary adds an owed row here, and silence is not coverage.

Nothing settled is pretended: V10, custody, G19 and the publication block remain on Route A, the honesty field keeps the full-TM constraint for any claim wider than the preview, and the condition-1 clause refuses a security-complete claim.

The coordinator is not treated as the sole owner, and the co-ownership case is handled as at v1: 'Threat-model authority + V1 coordinator (file 08 DR-003)… the coordinator may record jointly; it does not replace that authority', matching file 08's owner cell.

No silent SATISFIED: two occurrences, both negative. Header carries CANDIDATE-NOT-RECORDED and binds NOTHING. Implementation is not authorized; the single docs/v2/implementation/ occurrence is inside the condition-5 clause.
The COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md pin is current at 5229013ffd93eb539ee0f777491f996904c471efed550125f24553ebcce4b3cc, refreshed after the D-033 adoption at ac48808 rather than carried stale from v1.

The change set is confined to the advisory repair, the B-TRUST content repairs, the predecessor pins and the version bump: nine changed paths and six added, with the substantive ones at condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded and boundaries/6.

acceptanceScope.whatThisAcceptanceIs: An independent reviewer's judgement that the draft scoped preview threat model's bytes carry no blocker and no advisory I would raise, with the coverage limit at whatIDidNotCheck stated rather than implied.
whatItIsNot: Not owner recording. The artifact now forecloses this route by name, including the ACCEPT-verdict route, and this verdict is not that act.
Not a discharge of condition 1 for DR-003.
Not the full threat model, and not a security-complete claim, which the artifact refuses in terms.
Not a seal, not an application, and not closure of DR-003, which remains OPEN and HARD-BLOCKED on V10/custody, G19 and the publication block.
Not a replacement for the host-effect authorization contract, whose FC-C1 owner recording remains the precondition for any host doctor act.

verdictNote: ACCEPT, zero findings. My advisory landed with the retention I asked for. The unrequested B-TRUST repairs are the more substantive change and they fix a defect I did not catch at v1: I verified the boundary enumeration arithmetically and did not test whether the entries inside a boundary were of the kind their field names promise. I have recorded that miss, and I have recorded in whatIDidNotCheck that I applied the sharpened test only to the boundary the diff pointed me at rather than to all seven, so this acceptance carries a stated coverage limit rather than an implied one.
